_comment: Extra board keys for scripts/check-board-liveness.py to probe, BEYOND what it derives on its own. Normally empty: the probe derives seeds from the preserved captures, weekly/current.json and leaderboard.json, and derives ladder epochs from the epoch-shaped keys it has already seen plus a forward window. Add something here only when a value genuinely cannot be derived, and always with a source.
_rules: Every entry MUST carry a `source` saying who published the value and when. A value with no source is a hardcoded literal wearing a costume.
Do NOT pre-populate a seed before the ceremony that draws it has happened. An unconfirmed guess published here is a claim the site cannot support.
Remove entries once the probe can derive them (i.e. once a capture or a data file carries them). This file is a patch, not a registry.

board_key_shapes._comment: How to read the `version` half of a board key. The client sends the LADDER EPOCH, not the build. GameConfig.get_board_version() returns 'L' + LADDER_VERSION. Both shapes exist live: historical boards are build-shaped, current boards are epoch-shaped. Neither is an error.

ladder_epoch.meaning: current shape. The board key half the game actually sends. A build bump does NOT fork the board -- that was the point of the build-vs-ladder split.

build_version.meaning: historical shape, from before the build-vs-ladder split. Boards keyed this way are frozen history and must never be re-stamped.

current_ladder_epoch._comment: DECLARED, not derived -- pdoom1 still publishes no machine-readable epoch artifact, so this is the human channel standing in for one. It is populated because the game side has stated the value unambiguously and in writing, and because leaving it null made the site refuse to publish a board that real players were already scoring on. While it is set, every surface may name L4; if pdoom1 forks again and this is not updated, the site will confidently publish the WRONG board -- which is why the artifact ask below stays open until a workflow can read the epoch instead of a human typing it. The L3 -> L4 fork on 2026-08-07 is the second time this file has had to be hand-edited to keep up with a fork; the prior value was L3, declared 2026-07-30, and the L3 board (weekly-2026-w31, L3) is archived under preserved/2026-08-08-l3-epoch-close/.
current_ladder_epoch.source: pdoom1 v0.14.0 git tag message: 'Ladder L4. Featured seed weekly-2026-w32. Board key (weekly-2026-w32, L4).' Corroborated by the release's release_manifest.json, "ladder_version": "4". Game-side authority unchanged: GameConfig.get_board_version() returns 'L' + LADDER_VERSION. Positively verified 2026-08-08 by a read-only GET: (weekly-2026-w32, L4) held 9 entries from clients stamped v0.14.0 and v0.14.1 -- a positive check, since every WRONG key also returns ok:true with an empty board.
current_ladder_epoch.supersede_when: pdoom1 publishes the ladder epoch as a fetchable artifact (release asset or synced data file). Standing ask: PR #190's artifact request. Until then this value must be re-verified at every epoch fork, and a fork with no update here is a silent wrong-board bug.
current_ladder_epoch.verify_with: python scripts/check-board-liveness.py -- if the epoch here is wrong, populated boards on the real epoch show up as NEW ORPHAN rather than DEPLOYED.

extra_seeds.source: OBSERVED live on the score API 2026-07-31T17:15 AEST, immediately after the Gate 5 seed roll: the shipped v0.13.2 client is POSTing here. Not a guess and not pre-populated -- the ceremony had already happened and real entries existed before this line was written.
extra_seeds.why_needed: The probe DERIVES seeds from files that have already seen them (preserved captures, weekly/current.json, leaderboard.json, published-board.json). A brand-new seed is therefore invisible to it: on the first probe after the roll it checked 108 boards, never asked about w31, and reported 'OK: deployed board (weekly-2026-w30, L3)' -- a confident answer about the wrong board while two real players' scores sat unpublished. Epochs get a +2 lookahead; seeds get nothing equivalent because a seed is a drawn string, not a counter.
extra_seeds.remove_when: The publisher writes it into published-board.json, from which the probe derives it on subsequent runs. Safe to delete after the next successful publish -- but see the follow-up issue on making seed discovery not depend on a human noticing.

extra_seeds.source: pdoom1 v0.14.0 git tag message: 'Ladder L4. Featured seed weekly-2026-w32. Board key (weekly-2026-w32, L4).' CONFIRMED by observation, not taken on the tag's word alone: a read-only GET on 2026-08-08 found 9 entries on (weekly-2026-w32, L4) from clients stamped v0.14.0 and v0.14.1, so this is the key the shipped client is demonstrably POSTing to.
extra_seeds.why_needed: Same blind spot the w31 entry above records, hit a second time by the L3 -> L4 fork. The probe DERIVES seeds from files that have already seen them (preserved captures, weekly/current.json, leaderboard.json, published-board.json); a brand-new seed drawn for a new epoch is invisible to it until a publish writes it down. Epochs get a +2 lookahead; seeds get nothing equivalent, because a seed is a drawn string and not a counter. Without this line the probe would keep confidently reporting the closed (weekly-2026-w31, L3) board while nine real scores sat unpublished on w32.
extra_seeds.remove_when: The publisher writes it into published-board.json, from which the probe derives it on subsequent runs. Safe to delete after the next successful publish -- but note this is now the SECOND fork to need a manual line here, which is evidence for automating seed discovery rather than for repeating this edit.
